items.topic: Display layout: unified list vs sectioned groups
items.context: The ops tab currently renders a flat list of executions. Adding activities raises the question of how to combine two different data types in one view. A unified list interleaves them by timestamp, while sections keep them visually separated.

options.label: Unified chronological list
options.rationale: Interleave activities and executions sorted by timestamp. Simplest mental model — 'what's happening now' in one stream. Each item gets a small type indicator (icon or label). Recommended because operators care about recency, not data source.

options.label: Two collapsible sections (Activities / Executions)
options.rationale: Keep activities in a top section and executions below (or vice versa). Clearer separation, but operators must scan two lists to see 'what's active now'.

options.label: Tab-within-tab (sub-tabs for Activities vs Executions)
options.rationale: Adds a secondary tab bar inside the ops tab. Clean separation but hides one view at a time — defeats the purpose of a unified ops view.

items.context: Activities have many statuses and purposes. Showing all activities (including completed/failed ones from hours ago) could overwhelm the ops view. Need to decide what the default filter shows.

options.label: Active-only by default (pending, starting, running, needs_review)
options.rationale: Keeps the ops tab focused on 'what's happening now'. Users can expand the filter to see completed/failed activities. Recommended because it matches the ops mental model — you go here to see active work.

options.label: All activities from last 24 hours
options.rationale: Broader default view — shows recent history alongside active items. More context but potentially noisy.

options.label: All activities (same as executions — no time filter)
options.rationale: Consistent with how executions are shown today. Could be very long if many activities have accumulated.

items.topic: Visual differentiation between activities and executions
items.context: If activities and executions appear in the same list, users need to distinguish them at a glance. Both have similar status badges and timestamps, so an additional visual cue is needed.

options.label: Small type icon (e.g., bot icon for activity, play icon for execution)
options.rationale: Compact, doesn't add text clutter. Icons are already used in the sidebar for other purposes. Recommended for minimal visual footprint.

options.label: Text label badge ('Activity' / 'Execution')
options.rationale: Explicit and unambiguous, but adds visual weight to each row.

options.label: Subtle background tint or left border color
options.rationale: Visually distinct without extra elements. Could conflict with status-based coloring.

items.context: Clicking an execution navigates to its detail view via buildExecutionNodeId(). Activities don't have an equivalent detail node in the graph. Need to decide what clicking an activity does.

options.label: Navigate to the owning backlog item's node in the graph
options.rationale: Activities belong to a backlog item — navigating there gives full context. Leverages existing graph navigation. Recommended because it reuses existing infrastructure.

options.label: Open a lightweight activity detail popover/panel
options.rationale: Shows activity-specific info (purpose, run_id, timestamps) without leaving the ops tab. More informative but requires building a new component.

options.label: No click action (display-only)
options.rationale: Simplest to implement. Activities are informational — users can find details elsewhere.

items.text: The useAgentActivitiesStore is already initialized and polled every 5 seconds by GraphWorkspace. No new data fetching is needed — the ExecutionsTab (or renamed OpsTab) just needs to subscribe to the existing store alongside the execution store.

plan_updates: Created initial plan scaffold with problem statement, scope, technical context, and risk matrix. Implementation approach and phases left TBD pending display layout decision (d1).
